prompt: The query in the editor has one mistake. Fix it so that it answers this question: which promotions with a discount of at least 20 percent were not clearance campaigns? From the promotions table, list the promotions whose promo_name does not contain the word Clearance, written exactly like that with a capital C (a lower-case clearance does not count), and whose discount_pct is 20 or more. A promotion with no promo_name recorded (NULL) is not known to be a clearance campaign, so include it. A promotion with no discount_pct recorded does not count. Return three columns, in this order: promo_code, promo_name, discount_pct. Return one row per promotion. Any row order is fine. The visible data may not show the mistake; the hidden checks do.
hints: Next, write the row filter so it also keeps a promotion with no promo_name.

NOT LIKE on a missing name is unknown, not true, so the query drops the promotion with no promo_name. Keep it with an extra test joined by OR, in brackets so the discount test still applies to every row.
starter_sql:
SELECT promo_code, promo_name, discount_pct
FROM promotions
WHERE promo_name NOT LIKE '%Clearance%' AND discount_pct >= 20
why_this_works: OR promo_name IS NULL keeps the promotion with no name, which NOT LIKE alone drops because a comparison with NULL is unknown; the brackets keep the discount test on both.
